COMPLETE EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing executed)

========================================================================
0. OBJECTIVE AND FIXED REQUIREMENTS
========================================================================
Question: "For commonsense evaluations, will FuseLLM outperform Llama-2 on standard benchmarks Commonsense (CS) (zero-shot)?"

Answer target: determine, under a controlled reproduction, whether a FuseLLM model strictly outperforms the same-size Llama-2 base model on a fixed zero-shot commonsense (CS) multiple-choice suite, using mean accuracy over a fixed six-benchmark suite as the primary decision statistic.

Fixed task-level requirements (taken as given, not modifiable):
- setup_2 and setup_9 (iclr2024/18013/1). Neither is defined in any file in /workspace (recon found only task.json, whose track.md is a note, not source). Per explicit instruction they are treated as fixed requirements and mapped to the paper's two primary comparisons; this mapping is an EXPLICIT ASSUMPTION (A1), not a confirmed fact.
- No execution: this is a design-only task; any "checks" below are design-level verification steps, not claims of having run anything.

========================================================================
1. FIXED DESIGN CHOICES (as confirmed with the researcher)
========================================================================
(1) Matched-size comparison only, fused-vs-base within each size, exact HF checkpoint IDs from the paper:
   - Comparison A (7B):  fusellm/FuseLLM-7B  vs  meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf
   - Comparison B (13B): fusellm/FuseLLM-13B vs  meta-llama/Llama-2-13b-hf
   - Optional reference (not a decision input): openlm-research/open_llama_7b_v2 (OpenLLaMA-7B), the second fusion source, to contextualize where the gain comes from.
   - Cross-size comparisons (FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-13B) are explicitly OUT of scope.
(2) Primary CS suite of six (fixed): HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-easy, PIQA, OpenBookQA, BoolQ. Sensitivity analysis (Section 5) covers adding/removing ARC-challenge and CommonsenseQA.
(3) Single pinned version of EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness (fixed git commit, pinned at install time), num_fewshot=0 on every task, multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking, greedy/deterministic decoding; identical dtype/batch/max-length/templates for both models.
(4) Decision rule: primary = (FuseLLM mean CS) - (Llama-2 mean CS) > 0 on simple mean over the fixed six; secondary = per-benchmark win/loss margin table; optional = per-item stratified bootstrap 95% CI / paired-difference inference.
(5) Controls: same harness commit; same hardware/dtype/batch/max-seqlen; fixed per-dataset splits (Section 3).

========================================================================
2. RATIONALE FOR THE KEY CHOICES
========================================================================
- Matched size, fused-vs-base: FuseLLM is produced by continuing from a Llama-2 base under a distribution-fusion objective; the paper's claim is that the fused model beats the base it started from at the same size. Across-size comparison would confound capacity with fusion effect.
- Multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking, not generation: all six CS tasks are closed-form multiple choice (choose one of 2-4 options). The standard protocol scores each option continuation under the model and takes the max; this avoids decoding variance and makes scoring fully deterministic.
- Greedy/deterministic single run is sufficient (one of the confirmed fixed choices; state why): with num_fewshot=0 and log-likelihood ranking, the score is a deterministic function of the frozen weights and the fixed template. There is no sampling, hence no seed-induced variance, so a single run is the full run; any residual nondeterminism (kernel/order) is numerical noise at <0.01 accuracy level and should be controlled by running both models in the same process/hardware. Dataset sampling (e.g., HellaSwag's internal subsetting) is fixed by the harness/dataset files, not by an eval seed.
- Simple (unweighted) mean over six as primary: this is the paper's and the field's convention ("average over commonsense benchmarks"); it treats each benchmark equally and matches how the original tables were aggregated. Weighting by item count is reported as a robustness note but not used as the decision statistic.
- Exact checkpoint IDs: the HF repos fusellm/FuseLLM-7B and fusellm/FuseLLM-13B are the paper-reported released weights; Llama-2-hf are the base checkpoints the fusion continues from.

========================================================================
3. EVALUATION PROTOCOL (exact specification)
========================================================================
Harness: EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness, ONE pinned commit (commit hash recorded), run identically for all four models on the same host. Task names (v0.4.x canonical, to be verified at design-check time — Section 6):
   - hellaswag        (dataset split: validation; ~10,042 items; harness evaluates the LC subset ~6,653) | metric acc_norm (length-normalized)
   - winogrande       (validation; 1,267)                                                               | metric acc_norm
   - arc_easy         (validation; 2,376)                                                               | metric acc_norm
   - piqa             (validation; 1,838)                                                               | metric acc_norm
   - openbookqa       (test; 500)                                                                       | metric acc_norm
   - boolq            (validation; 3,270)                                                               | metric acc  (binary true/false; harness metric differs from 4-way MC)
   Sensitivity-only (not decision): arc_challenge (validation; 1,172), commonsense_qa (validation; 1,221).

Protocol for both models on every task — identical:
   - num_fewshot = 0 on every task (zero-shot by construction; no in-context exemplars, no demonstrations).
   - Scoring: multiple-choice log-likelihood ranking (max over option continuations), with identical normalization mode as the harness default for the metric reported (record acc_norm vs acc per task and keep metric constant across models).
   - Decoding: greedy (temperature=0) / no sampling; no generation is used for MC scoring; any harness-internal or optional open-ended task would cap max_new_tokens; for the six fixed MC tasks no max_new_tokens applies (log-likelihood only), but set a uniform max_seq_len (e.g., 2048) for all models.
   - dtype = same for all models (bf16 where supported, else fp16); batch size identical (set by harness batch arg, e.g., batch_size=8 per device for 7B, smaller for 13B — but identical between the two models within a size comparison); same prompt templates (harness defaults for each task, unchanged); same truncation/max-length policy.
   - Both models in a comparison run in the same environment session to hold numerical/hardware state constant.

========================================================================
4. ANALYSIS PLAN / DECISION RULE
========================================================================
For each size s in {7B, 13B} compute:
   mean_CS(FuseLLM_s) = (1/6) * sum over the six fixed tasks of task accuracy
   mean_CS(Llama2_s)  = same over the identical task set/splits/metrics
   delta_s = mean_CS(FuseLLM_s) - mean_CS(Llama2_s).

Decision (primary): "FuseLLM outperforms Llama-2 on CS (zero-shot)" = delta_s > 0 for the size under test. Report delta to 3 decimals; a strictly positive mean is the pass condition (the paper's claim is a strict improvement on the average).

Secondary evidence (always reported): per-benchmark table of accuracies for both models, win/loss/tie count across the six tasks, and margin per task; also report weighted-by-item-count mean as a robustness check.

Optional statistical layer (design includes it; whether it gates the answer is a stated choice):
   - Per-item stratified bootstrap: resample items within each benchmark (stratified so each benchmark contributes its same weight), recompute the six-benchmark mean for both models per resample; form a 95% CI on delta via the bootstrap percentile. Report CI and the proportion of resamples with delta>0 (a paired-difference probability). With only six benchmark means, a paired test over benchmark-level numbers has n=6 and is underpowered, so item-level stratified bootstrap is the appropriate significance instrument; it is OPTIONAL because the zero-shot deterministic protocol is not stochastic, and the field's standard is a point-average comparison without formal significance testing.
   - State clearly: the primary decision is the deterministic mean comparison; the bootstrap is reported as confidence quantification and does not change the decision rule.

========================================================================
5. SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS (confirmed fixed choice)
========================================================================
Report the full fixed-six result, then repeat the mean computation under:
   (a) +ARC-challenge (six -> seven: HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC-e, ARC-c, PIQA, OBQA, BoolQ) — mirrors the LLaMA-paper "Commonsense Reasoning" group;
   (b) +CommonsenseQA (six -> seven, replacing none: add CSQA);
   (c) +ARC-challenge + CommonsenseQA (eight).
State in the writeup whether delta_s sign/magnitude is robust across (six, seven-a, seven-b, eight). This guards the U2 boundary uncertainty (which sub-benchmarks constitute CS) by showing the conclusion's stability rather than asserting one canonical list. The fixed decision rule uses the six; sensitivity informs interpretation only.

========================================================================
6. FEASIBILITY CHECKS (design-level; NOT carried out, NOT claims of execution)
========================================================================
Listed steps that a real run must pass before trusting scores; each is a verification, not an experiment:
   (a) Harness task-name resolution: install pinned lm-eval, run `lm_eval --tasks hellaswag,winogrande,arc_easy,piqa,openbookqa,boolq ... --show_config`-style listing to confirm all six (plus arc_challenge, commonsense_qa) resolve to the intended tasks and report the intended metric (acc_norm/acc). Record the exact commit+task config as an artifact.
   (b) Split verification: confirm harness loads HellaSwag/WinoGrande/ARC-e/PIQA/BoolQ from validation, OpenBookQA from test, and confirm item counts approximately equal the values in Section 3 (they change with dataset version; record the versions). Mismatched splits would invalidate cross-model comparisons — both models must use identical splits.
   (c) Checkpoint correspondence: verify each HF repo ID resolves to the paper's released weights (FuseLLM-7B/13B from fusellm/*; Llama-2-7b/13b-hf from meta-llama/*), confirm config params/arch (7B: 32 layers/hidden 4096; 13B: 40 layers/hidden 5120), and confirm FuseLLM-13B's fusion source combination as reported in the paper (assumption A2: Llama-2-13B + OpenLLaMA-7B). If any checkpoint is unavailable (e.g., due to gated access/license), note it as a blocker in the writeup rather than substituting another model.
   (d) Determinism sanity: run a single model on a small task twice (same commit, same host) and confirm identical scores (to recorded precision) before the full matrix; this validates the "one deterministic run suffices" claim on the actual environment.
   (e) Resource budget estimate for the run (design note): ~15k log-likelihood items for the six-task suite per model; 4 models -> ~60k item evaluations; 7B/13B GPU or CPU inference with bf16. Record batch size and wall-clock expectation in the run card, but this is design context, not a result.

========================================================================
7. ASSUMPTIONS (explicit) vs FIXED REQUIREMENTS
========================================================================
Fixed (given, not open to change): setup_2 and setup_9 as task requirements; matched-size-only; six-benchmark primary suite; single pinned harness + num_fewshot=0 + log-likelihood ranking + greedy; mean>0 as primary decision rule; controls in Section 3/5; design-only (no execution).
Assumptions (my reading, to be re-confirmed only if new source appears):
   A1. setup_2 / setup_9 map to the paper's two primary zero-shot CS comparisons — FuseLLM-7B vs Llama-2-7B (setup_2) and FuseLLM-13B vs Llama-2-13B (setup_9). Not verifiable from the workspace; labelled per instruction as assumption, not fact.
   A2. FuseLLM identity and fusion sources as in arXiv:2310.06201 (FuseLLM-7B = Llama-2-7B + OpenLLaMA-7B; FuseLLM-13B = Llama-2-13B + OpenLLaMA-7B), and the 'Llama-2' comparator is the corresponding meta-llama/Llama-2-<size>-hf checkpoint.
   A3. The released HF checkpoints (fusellm/FuseLLM-7B, fusellm/FuseLLM-13B) are the faithful, paper-matched artifacts; no re-training is performed in this design.
   A4. CS = the six fixed multiple-choice commonsense benchmarks with the specified splits as the operative definition; the question's listed candidates are satisfied by this set, and boundary membership (BoolQ, ARC-c, CSQA) is handled by sensitivity analysis.
   A5. Zero-shot = zero in-context demonstrations via num_fewshot=0; 'standard benchmarks' refers to the released datasets as consumed by the pinned harness.

========================================================================
8. UNCERTAINTIES (do not block the locked design)
========================================================================
   U1. Exact content of setup_2/setup_9 is not present in the workspace (recon: only task.json). Binding rests on A1; if any file specifying them ever appears, A1 must be reconciled with it before the design is re-locked. Per instruction, A1 stands as the explicit working mapping.
   U2. CS sub-benchmark boundary (BoolQ/ARC-c/CSQA membership) — mitigated by the fixed-six primary rule + Section 5 sensitivity, so the answer is robust to this uncertainty.
   U3. Harness-version effects: different lm-eval commits change task names/metrics/num-fewshot defaults; fixed by pinning a single commit and recording its config (Section 6a).
   U4. Checkpoint availability/access: network is disabled in THIS sandbox, so nothing can be downloaded here; the design assumes the run would occur in a networked env with HF access. Documented as a blocker to flag, not a design change.
   U5. Whether 'outperform' must be formal-significance-gated for the task owner; design answers with deterministic mean>0 primary + per-benchmark secondary + optional bootstrap, and states which layer is decisive.

========================================================================
9. DELIVERABLE ARTIFACTS OF THE DESIGN (what a real run would produce)
========================================================================
(a) run card: harness commit, task list with split+counts+metric, model IDs, dtype, batch, seed policy (none needed - deterministic, justified in Section 2), date/host;
(b) per-model x per-task accuracy table (six + two sensitivity tasks) for all four models;
(c) delta_s for 7B and 13B on the fixed six with robustness across sensitivity variants;
(d) optional: stratified bootstrap CI on delta_s and P(delta>0);
(e) verdict per size using the primary rule, with the A1/A2 assumptions restated in the caption.

No experiment has been run; this is the complete locked design awaiting execution in an appropriate environment.
